answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce bond before placing jobs, with the bond held through a long dispute horizon. If an account is caught fabricating work or colluding, the protocol slashes its bond and rewards the reporter. Creating an ocean of sybil accounts therefore ties up capital in every identity, while coordinated fraud risks losing it. The attacker pays an opportunity cost that grows with each account. A ridge of honest, bonded participation makes sudden fake growth costly to sustain.
